answer: Bind each seat to one TPM attestation key from a distinct device, checked by a hardware attestation verifier that confirms the key was made inside a TPM and is absent from the registry atlas of used keys. If the same key or serial shows up on a second seat, both seats are revoked and their rewards are burned. An honest operator registers once with hardware they already own, while an attacker buying a TPM board at $40 each pays $40,000 for 1,000 fakes, since one board carries only one seat. A fake that reuses hardware falls from its comet arc to its nadir, while a real seat stays on course.
